historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blended base-case year 3-5 growth (organic recovery + steady tuck-in M&A), NOT a raw historical CAGR -- see growth_divergence_warning
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (39.8% 3yr / 27.3% 5yr) diverges massively (>30pp) from revenue (18.2%/17.7%) and EPS (12.3%/14.7%) CAGRs. This is a capital-structure artifact, not organic divergence: BRO issued a large follow-on common stock offering in 2025 specifically to help fund the ~$9.825B Accession acquisition (management's own Q2-2025 EBITDAC reconciliation footnote references 'interest income earned from the proceeds of the Company's follow-on common stock offering and senior notes issuance'), which mechanically inflated shareholders' equity far faster than earnings power grew. None of the raw CAGRs above are used directly as forward growth assumptions; the selected_growth_rate is a blended judgment documented in inputs.notes.

scenario_narratives.base: Organic growth stabilizes near BRO's own guided ranges as the soft cat-property cycle bottoms and E&S casualty strength partially offsets it, blended with continued tuck-in M&A; margin recovers gradually from the current integration-cost trough to a mid-cycle ~38% as the $30-40M of FY2026 synergies land and acquired-intangible amortization runs off per BRO's own disclosed schedule.
scenario_narratives.bull: E&S/specialty strength outruns property softness, cross-sell within the newly combined Retail/Specialty Distribution/Risk Strategies structure exceeds plan, synergies land ahead of schedule, and BRO resumes larger tuck-in M&A funded by strong post-integration FCF, pushing margin toward the high-30s/low-40s peers like Gallagher already achieve.
scenario_narratives.bear: The soft P&C cycle persists for years rather than bottoming in 2026, BRO continues underperforming large-cap peers on organic growth (raising genuine share-loss questions, not just market softness), the largest integration in company history disappoints on synergies and margin, and elevated acquisition leverage combined with weak growth pressures the equity story; the unexplained Retail-segment leadership departure is read as an early strain signal.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Brown & Brown is valued on a standard owner-FCF operating-company DCF, using a normalized FY0 revenue base (2x H1-2026 actual, $7,154M) rather than reported FY2025 revenue, because the ~$9.825B Accession/RSC Topco acquisition closed 2025-08-01 and FY2025 contains only five months of the combined company -- using it directly would understate the current run-rate of revenue, D&A and financing costs alike. The model separates two effects the market appears to be conflating: (1) a real, evidenced deceleration in organic growth (0% then -0.7% over the last two reported quarters, against a soft commercial P&C pricing cycle that has turned negative industry-wide for the first time in seven years) and (2) a mechanical, favorable D&A tailwind as BRO's own disclosed acquired-intangible amortization schedule runs off from $450M in 2026 to $395M by 2030, expanding the owner-FCF margin over the explicit horizon even before any assumed EBITDA margin recovery. A 10-year horizon is used because the margin is still visibly maturing under this schedule; capitalizing a 5-year, still-depressed margin would understate the business. Net debt (~$6.8B, ~2.9x EBITDA) is subtracted once at the end from an unlevered, EBIT-based flow that never double-counts interest expense inside the projections.
key_risks_to_valuation: Organic growth does not stabilize at the guided H2-2026 ranges and the soft P&C cycle persists multiple years, compounding with elevated post-Accession leverage

Accession/Risk Strategies/One80 integration takes longer than management's guidance to complete, with synergies undershooting the $30-40M FY2026 target and further margin compression beyond the Q2-2026 print

The disclosed forward amortization schedule is the single largest driver of margin expansion in the model over the explicit horizon; any further M&A that resets the intangible amortization clock (a real possibility given BRO's 625-deal history) would delay this tailwind
Unexplained Retail-segment leadership departure (Barrett Brown) during the integration window is a soft governance/succession signal not yet resolved
Interest-rate environment affects both the cost of BRO's largely floating/refinanced acquisition debt and the fiduciary-fund investment income embedded in 'Investment income and other income'

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 53.81-96.55
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via BRO_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2008-Q2 2026); BRO 10-K FY2025 and 10-Q Q2-2026 (BeautifulSoup-extracted text) for EBITDAC reconciliation, disclosed forward amortization schedule, balance sheet detail (total debt, cash, diluted shares) and effective tax rate

inputs.sbc_source: Q2-2026 10-Q cash flow statement, non-cash stock-based compensation add-back, H1-2026 ($49M) annualized to $98M; equity-award tax withholding ('Repurchase shares to fund tax withholdings for non-cash stock-based compensation', ~$27M H1) is a separate, smaller financing outflow not folded into the reconciliation figure BRO discloses -- included implicitly via the flat share count rather than double-subtracted from FCF
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% for a USD-denominated, investment-grade (BBB-area) insurance brokerage with elevated but serviceable acquisition leverage: ~4.5% risk-free (10yr UST run-rate) + ~5% levered equity-risk premium reflecting the post-Accession debt load (~2.9x net debt/EBITDA) and integration/organic-growth risk currently repricing the stock (52-week range $53.81-$96.55). No separate WACC premium is stacked on top of the bear-scenario growth/margin haircuts -- risk is charged once, through the discount rate for all three scenarios, and again through the scenario paths themselves for the growth/margin axis specifically, per section 7f.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are small relative to the flows (lease assets $274M / liabilities $248M+$? on a $29.9B balance sheet) and are left inside EBITDA/opex as reported (treatment A, no separate lease driver) -- BRO does not run a lease-heavy branch network comparable to a retailer; the operating-lease footnote confirms this is office space for producer teams, not a distinct economic driver.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (~$1-6M/quarter net income attributable to NCI on $230-290M attributable to the Company) and are left unadjusted; FY0 NOPAT is built off consolidated EBIT, not attributable-only, because the NCI slice is far below a materiality threshold that would change any scenario's per-share value by a cent.
inputs.notes:
MODEL CHOICE: routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md to the owner-FCF operating-company DCF. BRO is an asset-light insurance brokerage/agency -- it earns commissions and fees for placing/servicing policies on behalf of carriers, plus profit-sharing contingent commissions; it does NOT underwrite risk itself (no loss reserves held for its own account -- 'Losses and loss adjustment reserve' and 'Unearned premiums' on the balance sheet are pass-through fiduciary items relating to MGA/program business acting as an agent for carriers, not BRO's own underwriting exposure). It is therefore NOT a bank, insurer-underwriter, REIT or LIC, and does not route to residual-income, BVPS-compounding, AFFO or NAV models. Standard owner-FCF DCF applies.

FY0 / BASE REVENUE CHOICE: FY2025 reported revenue ($5,902M) is NOT used as the base because the ~$9.825B RSC Topco/Accession Risk Management Group acquisition closed 2025-08-01 -- FY2025 therefore contains only ~5 months of the acquired business layered onto a full year of legacy BRO, understating the current run-rate by roughly $1.25B of revenue and proportionally understating current D&A (acquired-intangible amortization) and interest expense (acquisition debt only partially outstanding for the year). Base revenue instead uses 2x H1-2026 actual revenue ($3,577M x 2 = $7,154M), which reflects a full year of the combined company at the current interest/D&A/organic-growth run-rate. This is the 'mid-cycle / normalized' treatment flagged as likely necessary: H1 revenue has run almost exactly 50% of full-year revenue in every pre-deal year (FY2023: 50.8%, FY2024: 50.7%), so the 2x-H1 annualization is a near-unbiased FY2026 estimate, not an extrapolation of a seasonally unusual half.

EBITDA MARGIN ANCHOR: uses FY2025's full-year disclosed EBITDAC-Adjusted margin of 35.9% (company non-GAAP: income before interest/tax/D&A/change-in-earnout, ex disposal gains, acquisition/integration costs and escrow mark-to-market) as the FY0 anchor rather than the H1-2026 actual (37.2% adjusted / 37.5% unadjusted), because H1 is seasonally the stronger half for margin (heavier Q1 contingent-commission recognition) and FY2025's full-year figure is the less noisy read on run-rate profitability. Q2-2026 alone showed margin compression to 35.7% (adjusted) from 36.7% a year earlier per management's own commentary -- consistent with a flat-to-slightly-down near-term margin path in the base case before synergy realization and integration completion lift it from FY2027 onward.

D&A PATH: BRO's FY2025 10-K discloses the forward amortization schedule for acquired intangibles explicitly -- $450M (2026), $431M (2027), $424M (2028), $406M (2029), $395M (2030) -- which is used directly for years 1-5 of every scenario (a rare case of company-disclosed forward D&A rather than an assumed flat percentage). This schedule is the single largest driver of owner-FCF margin expansion over the explicit horizon: D&A falls from ~7.0% of revenue in year 1 to ~3.4% by year 10 as acquired-intangible amortization runs off, even before any EBITDA margin improvement. This is why a 10-year horizon (not 5) is used -- the year-5 owner-FCF margin (roughly 22-24% in the base case) is still well below its matured level.

INTEREST: interest EXPENSE (not income) is the relevant item here -- BRO carries ~$6.8B of net debt post-Accession, not net cash, so the owner-FCF DCF's usual 'strip interest income' adjustment (for net-cash companies) does not apply. Interest expense correctly does NOT appear anywhere in the unlevered EBIT-based flows (dcf_engine.py builds EBITDA -> SBC -> D&A -> EBIT -> tax on EBIT -> NOPAT, never touching interest); the debt burden is captured once, via the net-debt deduction from enterprise value. This is standard unlevered DCF mechanics, not a special adaptation.

WORKING CAPITAL: BRO's commission/fee receivables and payables-to-carriers are roughly matched in an agency model (no large deferred-revenue balance like a subscription business -- deferred revenue is ~$127-132M, ~1.8% of revenue), so a small NEGATIVE working-capital capture (-3% of the revenue change) is used, reflecting modest net receivables growth on rising commissions -- not the positive capture used for prepaid/subscription models.

ORGANIC GROWTH STALL: per the Analysis JSON, organic growth was 0% (Q1-2026) and -0.7% (Q2-2026), well behind peers (Aon +5%, Marsh +5%, Gallagher +6%). The base-case growth path (4.0% year 1, ramping to 5.0% by years 3-5) is a BLENDED figure -- modest low-single-digit organic recovery (per BRO's own H2-2026 guidance of 1.5-2.5% Retail / 2-4% Specialty Distribution organic ex-contingents) PLUS BRO's continued steady tuck-in M&A pace (625+ deals since 1993), not a claim that organic growth alone reaccelerates to double digits. This blended figure sits well below BRO's own pre-Accession 3yr/5yr revenue and equity CAGRs (16.3%/15.0% revenue, 15.3%/14.0% equity for FY2019-24), which occurred during a hardening P&C pricing cycle now reversed to a soft market -- using the historical hard-cycle CAGR as a forward assumption would be exactly the error this build is designed to avoid.
inputs.historical_cagr_caveat: Raw FY2020-2025 and FY2022-2025 CAGRs (revenue 17.7%/18.2%, equity 27.3%/39.8%) are NOT used as growth-rate anchors: they are dominated by the Accession acquisition step-change and, for equity, by the large follow-on common stock offering issued in 2025 to help fund the deal -- both one-time capital-structure events, not repeatable organic or M&A-driven compounding. Pre-Accession (FY2019-2024) CAGRs of 15-18% are used instead as a ceiling/reference for what BRO's steady-state M&A-plus-organic engine can produce in a normal cycle, then discounted further because that period benefited from a hardening market that has now reversed to soft pricing.

bear.narrative: The soft commercial P&C pricing cycle (negative global rates for the first time in seven years, record reinsurance capital) persists for multiple years rather than bottoming in 2026, organic growth stays flat-to-slightly-positive as BRO continues to underperform Aon/Marsh/Gallagher (raising real questions about share loss, not just market softness), and the largest, most complex integration in company history (Accession/Risk Strategies/One80) takes longer than guided to digest -- synergies undershoot the $30-40M target and EBITDAC margin compresses further from the Q2-2026 print (35.7% adjusted, already down from 36.7%) rather than recovering. Elevated leverage (interest expense already roughly doubled YoY) combined with weak organic growth pressures the equity story, and the unexplained Retail-segment leadership departure (Barrett Brown) is read as an early signal of deeper organizational strain during the integration. No further debt-funded M&A is assumed; capital is directed to deleveraging.

base.narrative: Organic growth stabilizes at BRO's own H2-2026 guided ranges (Retail 1.5-2.5%, Specialty Distribution 2-4% ex-contingents) as the soft cat-property cycle bottoms and rising E&S casualty rates partially offset it, blended with BRO's continued steady tuck-in M&A pace (its 30+ year, 625+ deal playbook) to produce 4-5% total revenue growth -- well below the 15-18% pre-Accession hard-cycle CAGR and consistent with a reversed pricing cycle. Accession/Risk Strategies integration completes over 2026-2027, delivering the guided $30-40M of FY2026 synergies and lifting EBITDA margin gradually from a near-term trough (35.5%, reflecting the Q2-2026 compression management flagged) to a mid-cycle ~38% as integration costs roll off. Acquired-intangible amortization runs off per BRO's own disclosed schedule ($450M declining to $395M through 2030), mechanically expanding the owner-FCF margin over the explicit horizon even before EBITDA margin improves. Leverage (~2.9x net debt/EBITDA at close) is serviced from FCF without further equity issuance; no additional transformational M&A is assumed beyond normal tuck-ins.

bull.narrative: E&S/specialty casualty rate strength (a real, disclosed offsetting trend to declining cat-property pricing) more than compensates for the property softness, organic growth reaccelerates toward mid-to-high single digits as Risk Strategies/One80 cross-sell and referral flow within the decentralized model exceed plan, and BRO resumes its historical pace of larger tuck-in M&A funded by strong post-integration FCF. Synergies land ahead of the $30-40M FY2026 target and margin expands toward the high-30s/low-40s range peers like Gallagher already achieve, as the decentralized 190+-profit-center model proves it scales the largest deal in company history without diseconomies. Leverage de-levers faster than the base case on stronger FCF, supporting continued buybacks alongside tuck-ins.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 25% ceiling of the house default (to 30%) and bull trimmed to 25% because two consecutive quarters of actual reported organic growth (0%, then -0.7%) already confirm the bear axis is not merely a hypothetical risk -- it is the trailing print, against a soft-cycle backdrop management itself describes as a multi-quarter phenomenon (negative global commercial rates for the first time in seven years). The largest acquisition in company history is still mid-integration with real execution risk (an unexplained Retail-segment leadership departure during the integration window is a genuine, if soft, signal), and leverage (~2.9x net debt/EBITDA, interest expense roughly doubled YoY) reduces the margin for error if organic growth does not stabilize. Base is not reduced further because BRO's underlying moat (decentralized model, 30-year M&A track record, non-discretionary revenue) and management's specific guided organic ranges for H2-2026 are still the most probable single outcome; bull requires several things (cycle bottoming AND synergy overdelivery AND M&A resumption) to go right simultaneously, which is why it is held below the house default of 35%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
